boundary_evidence: NOT FROM tu_map. tools/tu_map.py reports the arm9 `main` module as UNDER-SEGMENTED -- one unit 0x20049f0..0x20707a4 with 2984 functions and 73 class labels -- so there is no tu_map boundary and no `tubuild.py create` candidate id. Every line below is hand-derived.

contiguous run 0x0203b4ac..0x0203b4dc: the two functions tile the span exactly, 0x18 + 0x18 = 0x30 = end-start, no hole and no tail (recomputed from config/arm9/symbols.txt). No foreign symbol lies inside it.
class-label homogeneity is total: both symbols are _ZN7fBase_c9SceneNode*, i.e. members of the NESTED class ActorBase::SceneNode, and there are no others anywhere in the image.

SEPARATE FROM ActorBase'S OWN TU, and this is the load-bearing negative. These are the only two _ZN7fBase_c* functions outside the class's main run at 0x02043444..0x02043f4c, and they sit 0x8000 bytes below it. A single object's .text is placed contiguously by the linker, so one TU cannot occupy two regions 0x8000 apart -- merging them into arm9/ActorBase would require exactly that. arm9/ActorBase is independently LINK-VERIFIED over 0x02043444..0x02043dec without them, which confirms the split from the other side.

neighbourhood attribution: 0x0203b2xx-0x0203b4xx is the intrusive-list primitive stretch -- func_0203b20c, func_0203b244, func_0203b27c and func_0203b3c0 all live there, and every one of them is called from ActorBase's own members (AfterInitResources, AfterCleanupResources, func_02043880). This pair sits at the TOP of that stretch, which is consistent with a scene-graph-node TU adjacent to the list code it is built on.

neighbours on both sides carry a different label: func_0203b438 ends at 0x0203b4ac below, and _ZN4cstd5atan2E5Fix12IiES1_ begins at 0x0203b4dc above -- a cstd math routine, which is certainly a different TU.

CONFIDENCE IS medium, NOT high, and the reason is stated rather than hidden: the run is only two functions and BOTH its neighbours are unlabelled-or-unrelated, so nothing positively attributes the functions immediately below it to this same TU. The lower boundary at 0x0203b4ac is therefore a floor supported by a label change, not by a positive claim about func_0203b438. The upper boundary at 0x0203b4dc is strong (a cstd template instantiation cannot share a TU with an actor scene node). It is entirely possible the original .cpp also contained some of the list primitives below; this entry licenses only what it can defend.

static-initialiser attribution: no help. main has 23 sinits / 23 .ctor entries, sinit_vs_tu 'ok', corroborated=false, and this run touches no dynamically-initialised static storage -- the object emits no .init, no .bss and no .data.
notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main. The entry was built through tubuild.build_manifest_entry so the schema is the tool's own; boundary_confidence and boundary_evidence were then replaced with hand-derived values.

This is the 0x30-byte OUTLIER of the ActorBase assignment: 25 _ZN7fBase_c* function symbols exist in the image, 23 in the main run (see arm9/ActorBase) and these 2 here. include/ActorBase.h now records the split.

BOTH MEMBERS ARE extern "C" RATHER THAN REAL ActorBase::SceneNode:: METHODS, on purpose. The mangled names say they are members of a class nested inside ActorBase, but include/ActorBase.h spells that type at top level as `ActorBase_SceneNode`. Making real methods possible means nesting it and declaring a constructor on the nested type -- which makes ActorBase's implicit default constructor non-trivial, in a header 1,393 enrolled C++ TUs include, several of whose classes have compiler-generated constructors that would then have to call it. That is the implicit-constructor hazard, and it deserves its own change and its own sweep rather than riding on a 0x30-byte TU. FOLLOW-UP, not a defect.

The type used is ActorBase.h's `ActorBase_SceneNode` (0x14 bytes, five fields) rather than the auto-generated include/ActorBase__SceneNode.h (0x10 bytes, four fields), which is the less complete of the tree's two spellings and is now referenced by nothing else. Reset() clears only the first four words and deliberately leaves the owner back-pointer at +0x10 alone; ActorBase's constructor writes that one.
